answer: Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 164 answers need 164 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Because the glacier index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the vault audit republishes the full set. Reusing one run across aliases collides on the cipher identifier and voids the later submissions, and therefore the operator pays for 164 runs and collects one. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
